messages.app.offline: Your browser is offline. Keep this tab open to create invoice links and review invoices. Checking payments needs a connection to your RPC.
messages.pay.offlineCheck: Chain verification is unavailable while offline. Reconnect and check again.
messages.create.draft.keep: Keep an encrypted draft in this tab
messages.create.draft.hint: To recover edits after a reload, keep an encrypted draft and reopen it with the same seller keys. The draft holds the form as you typed it, including the memo, the line item text, quantities and prices. With Privacy-minimal invoice on, the memo and line item text are left out; the other fields are still kept. Invoice passphrases are not saved and must be entered again. There is no timer: the draft stays in this tab until you close the tab (a browser may restore a closed tab with its draft), the invoice is created, you remove it, or the seller keys are cleared.
messages.create.draft.available: This tab has an unfinished encrypted invoice for these seller keys.
messages.create.draft.saved: Latest edits saved in this tab.
messages.create.draft.saveFailed: The latest edits could not be saved. Keep this tab open. Editing again retries the save.
messages.create.draft.openFailed: The saved draft could not be opened. Remove it to save a new draft.
messages.create.draft.removeFailed: The browser could not remove the saved draft. Try again.
messages.app.checks.title: Browser self-checks
messages.app.checks.limits: These checks are not an independent verification of application code integrity, wallet or RPC authenticity, payment safety, chain settlement or key recovery. No network request is made.
messages.app.checks.secure.fail: This page is not in a secure context (HTTPS or localhost). Browsers withhold WebCrypto, camera and clipboard access outside one, so parts of GhostPay can fail. Open the app from its https:// address.
messages.app.checks.secure.unavailable: This browser does not report whether this page is in a secure context. Treat the browser as unsupported and use a current version.
messages.app.checks.digest.fail: WebCrypto SHA-256 returned a wrong result or an error. Do not rely on this browser for keys, invoices or payments. Update it or use another browser.
messages.app.checks.digest.unavailable: WebCrypto is not available here. Browsers omit it outside a secure context and in outdated versions. Features that use it, such as encrypted local records and exports, can fail.
messages.app.checks.storage.fail: Site storage did not return or remove the test value correctly. Settings and local records may be lost or out of date. Export your backups and check this browser's site-storage settings.
messages.app.checks.storage.unavailable: This browser refused site storage, for example because site data is blocked or storage is full. Settings and local records may not be kept. Allow site storage, or export your backups before you close the tab.
messages.app.checks.indexeddb.fail: The browser database (IndexedDB) did not store, return or delete the test record correctly, or did not respond. The optional saved key vault and encrypted local records may be lost or unreadable. Export your backups and check this browser's site-data settings.
messages.app.checks.indexeddb.unavailable: This browser refused its site database (IndexedDB), for example because site data is blocked. The optional saved key vault, tags and reconciliation records may not be kept after you close the tab. Export your backups first.
messages.requestFile.downloadHint: This file gives its holder the same access as the invoice link. It adds no encryption. Share any passphrase separately. Downloads, backups and device sync may keep a copy.
messages.requestFile.downloadFailed: The request file could not be downloaded. Try again or use the original invoice link.
messages.requestFile.summary: Scan an invoice QR or open a request file
messages.requestFile.label: Payment request file
messages.requestFile.hint: Choose a GhostPay request file (up to 24 KiB). It is read locally. Review it before opening payment details; selecting a file does not connect a wallet or submit a payment.
messages.requestFile.ready: Request file is ready for review.
messages.requestFile.tooLarge: Request file exceeds the 24 KiB size limit.
messages.requestFile.invalid: Cannot read this request file. Choose a valid GhostPay request file.
messages.settings.title: Settings
messages.settings.notice.plaintext: Settings are kept in this browser in plain text, including RPC URLs. Do not put a URL there that contains a secret you would not store in plain text. No key is ever stored.
messages.settings.rpc.hint: Only https:// and wss:// are accepted, with no username or password. The chain id is verified when the endpoint is used. No default RPC is built in.
messages.settings.rpc.connected: Connected. The endpoint reports the expected chain id.
messages.settings.rpc.failed: Failed: the endpoint is unreachable or reports a different chain.
messages.settings.rpc.secondary.label: {chain} second RPC URL (optional)
messages.settings.rpc.secondary.hint: A different provider. Scans compare it with the main RPC and withhold the checkpoint when they disagree.
messages.settings.relayer.label: Relayer URL (optional)
messages.settings.relayer.hint: https only. The relayer sees the one-time address, destination, token, amount and timing of each sweep it handles.
messages.settings.delay.range: Each payment is delayed between {min, number} and {max, number} seconds.
messages.settings.lock.idleLabel: Idle lock after minutes without activity
messages.settings.lock.keysHint: After this many minutes without a click or key press, local tags lock. Seller keys are wiped from memory at the same time only when a copy survives the wipe: all three imported keys, keys whose downloaded keystore you verified under Seller keys, or keys whose vault is still saved in this browser. Keys with no backup, or with only an unverified download, stay loaded, with a warning, until you back them up, wipe them or close the tab.
messages.settings.lock.summary: Locks after {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} without activity.
messages.settings.theme.label: Theme
messages.settings.autoclear.label: Remove the invoice from the address bar after reading it
messages.settings.invoiceClipboard.label: Clear copied invoice links and other sensitive data
messages.settings.invoiceClipboard.hint: After the selected delay, GhostPay checks the clipboard text before attempting to clear it. Your browser may block access.
messages.settings.pins.label: Pinned seller signing keys (one per line)
messages.settings.pins.hint: Only keys you pin are described as pinned. Get them from the seller over a channel you trust.
messages.settings.pins.count: {count, plural, =0 {No pinned signer keys} one {# pinned signer key} other {# pinned signer keys}}
messages.settings.storageUnavailable: Browser storage is unavailable, so these settings apply to this tab only.
messages.settings.changedElsewhere: Settings changed in another tab. The changed values are shown here now. Check them before you save.
messages.settings.error.pins: Pinned signer keys must be 66 hexadecimal characters starting with 02 or 03, one per line.
messages.settings.error.lock: Lock timeout must be 1 to 240 minutes.

messages.i18n.loadFailed: The selected language could not be loaded. English is shown instead.
messages.settings.exchange.title: Move settings to your other devices
messages.settings.exchange.description: Copy saved settings to another device of your own. You choose what goes into the QR; only preferences are selected at first. Private keys, passphrases, backups and vault contents are never included. Every import is reviewed before anything is applied.
messages.settings.exchange.exportHint: Choose what to include. Only saved settings are exported.
messages.settings.exchange.section.preferences: Preferences (delay, idle lock, theme, address bar)
messages.settings.exchange.includedNothing: Nothing is selected. Select at least one section.
messages.settings.exchange.prefsValue: delay {min}–{max} s, idle lock {minutes} min, theme {theme}, remove invoice from address bar: {autoclear}
messages.settings.exchange.noRelayer: none (the other device can choose to clear its relayer)
messages.settings.exchange.privacyWarning: RPC and relayer URLs are not keys, but they are private: they show which providers you use, and a URL often contains your account or API key. The QR contains the full URLs. Show it only to your own device's camera, never in public.
messages.settings.exchange.tooLarge: This selection is too large for one QR code. Select fewer sections and move the rest with a second QR.
messages.settings.exchange.exportFailed: This selection cannot be exported. Check that the saved RPC URLs and pinned keys are valid, save the settings again, and retry.
messages.settings.exchange.reviewHint: Nothing has been applied and no imported endpoint has been contacted. Tick each section you want; sections that change endpoints or trust start unticked.
messages.settings.exchange.noChanges: No changes: this device already has these settings.
messages.settings.exchange.rpcMergeHint: Only the chains listed are replaced; endpoints for other chains stay as they are.
messages.settings.exchange.relayerTrustHint: The relayer sees the one-time address, destination, token, amount and timing of each sweep it handles. Change it only to a relayer you trust.
messages.settings.exchange.signersTrustHint: Pinning a signing key means trusting the invoices it signs. Imported keys stay untrusted until you tick each one. Compare each key with the seller's before you pin it.
messages.settings.exchange.signersUnchanged: {count, plural, =0 {No keys are pinned on both devices.} one {# key is already pinned here.} other {# keys are already pinned here.}}
messages.settings.exchange.signersRemove: {count, plural, one {Also unpin # key that the other device does not pin} other {Also unpin # keys that the other device does not pin}}
messages.settings.exchange.selectSomething: Tick at least one changed section to apply.
messages.settings.exchange.confirmBody: These changes alter which RPC endpoints, relayer and signing keys this device trusts, or weaken its protection. Check each one. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
messages.settings.exchange.confirmRpc: {section}: {chain} (chain {chainId}) {from} → {to}. This endpoint sees which addresses you check and could misreport payments.
messages.settings.exchange.applyFailed: Nothing was changed: the imported settings could not be applied as reviewed. Import the code again.
messages.sweep.title: Sweep
messages.sweep.choosePayment: Choose a payment to sweep from Scan and receive.
messages.sweep.keysGone: Your keys are no longer in memory. Load them again in Seller keys.
messages.sweep.vaultCancelledKeys: Vault check cancelled because seller keys changed.
messages.sweep.paymentsDisabledChain: Payments are disabled on this chain: no deployment manifest is loaded.
messages.sweep.balanceUnknown: unknown (an RPC for this chain is required)
messages.sweep.noManifest: Payments disabled on this chain: no deployment manifest is loaded.
messages.sweep.tokenNotAllowed: This token is not on the allowlist. It will not be swept from here.
messages.sweep.payerFollow.title: The payer can follow this sweep
messages.sweep.payerFollow.body: The payer knows the one-time address. When you move its funds, the destination and everything else that address has received or will receive are public and linkable. Use a fresh destination for each sweep, and avoid an address already known to be yours if you do not want to link those funds. A relayer also sees your IP address (hashed by the reference relayer for rate limits, but visible to the operator and any proxy), amount and timing. Your stealth key is derived in memory for this action and is never shown or stored.
messages.sweep.destination.label: Destination address (your own wallet)
messages.sweep.vaultPass.label: Vault passphrase (required for each sweep action)
messages.sweep.vaultPass.hint: Checked against the encrypted vault that holds the seller keys loaded now: the one they were unlocked from, saved to or found in, which stays in memory for this session even if the saved vault is deleted. It is cleared after every action. Do not let your browser save it.
messages.sweep.vaultError: Could not check encrypted vault storage, so sweep signing is disabled until storage is available.
messages.sweep.feeLegend: How to pay the network fee
messages.sweep.modeRelayer: Through the relayer (fee deducted from the amount; needs a permit-capable token)
messages.sweep.modeDirect: Directly (the one-time address must hold native coin for gas)
messages.sweep.relayerNeeds: Relayer sweeps need a relayer URL in Settings and a token with ERC-2612 permit. Use a direct sweep otherwise.
messages.sweep.checkExplorer: Check it on your RPC or a block explorer you trust before relying on it.
messages.sweep.pendingBlocksSigning: A sweep from this address may still be pending. Check its status before signing anything new.
messages.sweep.attempt.unknownDirect: The signed transaction was handed to your RPC but its result is unknown. It may already be on the network, so a new sweep is disabled. When available below, a replacement uses the same nonce and retains every earlier transaction hash.
messages.sweep.attempt.unknownRelayed: The signed order was handed to the relayer but its result is unknown. It can still execute until {deadline}; it counts as expired only {minutes} minutes after that. Signing a new one is disabled until then.
messages.sweep.attempt.expiredBody: The order's nonce was still unused after its deadline, so it can no longer execute and moved nothing. You can sign again.
messages.sweep.attempt.refusedBody: The relayer reported that it refused the order before sending it. This relies on the relayer's report; the signed order stays valid until {deadline}. You can sign again.
messages.sweep.attempt.replacedBody: No receipt was found for this hash or for any earlier attempt with the same nonce, but that nonce is already used in a finalized block, so this transaction can never be included. Another transaction with that nonce (for example one signed in another tab) was included instead. Check the address on a block explorer. You can sign again.
messages.sweep.permit.ok: The permit checks passed: the token will accept this signature for exactly the sweep amount.
messages.sweep.permit.alreadyAllowed: An allowance already covers this sweep, so the permit is skipped and the sweep uses the allowance. Nothing else is needed.
messages.sweep.permit.nonceConsumed: This permit was already used or replaced (its nonce is spent) and no allowance covers the sweep. Nothing was moved. It will not be retried automatically.
messages.sweep.permit.failed: This permit is not valid for this sweep (an invalid signature, or a permit that was already used), so the sweep was not sent with it. Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically.
messages.sweep.permit.simulationFailed: The relayer's pre-broadcast simulation failed while a permit was in use, so it refused the order before sending it. The cause may be the permit (an invalid signature, a permit that was already used, or a token without standard permit support) or the token transfer itself (for example, a token that takes a fee on transfer). Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically.
messages.sweep.permit.expired: The relayer reported that the permit had already expired, so it refused the order before sending it. Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically. Sign a new sweep.
messages.sweep.permit.unsupported: The relayer reported that this token does not accept standard ERC-2612 permits, so it refused the order. Nothing was moved and nothing will be retried automatically.
messages.sweep.permit.valueTooLow: The relayer reported that the signed permit did not cover the full amount, so it refused the order before sending it. Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically. Sign a new sweep.
messages.sweep.permit.noAllowance: The relayer reported that the stealth address has no allowance and no usable permit, so it refused the order. Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically.
messages.sweep.permit.ownerFailureLimit: The relayer refused this order because there were too many failed sweep attempts from this address in the last hour. Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically. Wait before signing again.
messages.sweep.permit.directFallback: You can sweep directly instead: the stealth address then pays the network fee itself and needs a little native coin for gas.
messages.sweep.note.pendingRelayed: The order has not executed yet, and no finalized block is far enough past its deadline to treat it as expired. It may still execute; check again later.
messages.sweep.note.pendingDirect: No receipt found for this hash yet. That does not mean it was not sent; check again later.
messages.sweep.note.noRpc: No RPC is configured for this chain, so the status was not checked. The outcome is still unknown.
messages.sweep.note.checkFailed: The status check failed. The outcome is still unknown; check again later.
messages.sweep.note.lockChanged: This sweep's record changed while the status was being checked, so the result was not applied. Check again.
messages.sweep.resign.hint: Use this only if the network most likely never accepted this transaction (your RPC failed at handoff or no longer reports any recorded transaction). The replacement goes to the destination entered above with the same nonce {nonce}, so at most one of them can ever be included; Check status looks for each of them. It is not a fee bump, so it does not speed up a transaction the network already holds.
messages.sweep.resign.limit: Replacement limit reached. Check the recorded transactions until their outcome is resolved; signing stays locked.
messages.sweep.note.rpcForgot: The configured RPC no longer reports any recorded transaction. This does not prove they were dropped everywhere. When available below, a replacement uses the same nonce; a new sweep stays locked.
messages.sweep.resign.button: Review a replacement with the same nonce
messages.sweep.resign.nothingPending: There is no pending direct sweep to replace. Check its status.
messages.sweep.direct.reviewTitle: Check this sweep before you sign it
messages.sweep.direct.maxGas: Network fee: at most {fee} (gas limit {gas}, at most {price} gwei per unit of gas).
messages.sweep.direct.l1Reserve: Also kept back for the OP Stack L1 data and operator fees: {reserve}.
messages.sweep.direct.leftoverNative: The fee comes out of this balance. Of the {kept} kept back, whatever the network does not charge stays at the one-time address; it is usually too little to sweep again.
messages.sweep.direct.feeFromNative: The fee is paid from the native coin at the one-time address, not from the {asset} sent. Unused fee coin stays there.
messages.sweep.direct.validFor: Signing signs exactly this transaction with the one-time key, without a wallet prompt. The review is valid for {minutes} minutes; after that, or if anything here changes, review it again.
messages.sweep.direct.reviewDryRunUnavailable: Your RPC could not dry-run this transfer, so a transfer that fails would not be caught before it is sent, and its network fee would be lost.
messages.sweep.gasFunding.title: Funding gas can link your wallet to this payment
messages.sweep.gasFunding.body: A direct sweep of a token pays its network fee in native coin from the one-time address. Sending that coin from a wallet you use elsewhere publicly links that wallet to this payment and to whoever paid it. Use a relayer you trust, ask payers to include a gas buffer, or fund gas only from an address with no other history.
messages.sweep.dryRunUnavailable: Your RPC could not dry-run this sweep, so it was signed and sent without that check. Check the transaction on a block explorer.
messages.sweep.journalBroken.title: Signing disabled in this tab
messages.sweep.journalBroken.body: The sweep attempt record in this tab is unavailable or invalid. Signing stays disarmed; a sweep may still be pending. Check the address on a block explorer before trying again in a new tab.
messages.sweep.balanceRead.button: Read balance from the Settings RPC
messages.sweep.balanceRead.warning: Your scan settings require the private path, so the balance of this one-time address is not read automatically. Reading it goes directly to the RPC in Settings, not through your private scan path. The provider learns this address, the token contract for a token balance, and the connecting IP address. These app settings do not route this request through Tor. Any Tor protection depends on your browser or network setup.
messages.sweep.balanceRead.note: The balance of this one-time address is read only when you click the button below. Clicking sends this address and, for a token balance, the token contract to the RPC provider in Settings. The provider also sees the connecting IP address. The request goes directly to that RPC, not through your private scan path. These app settings do not route this request through Tor. Any Tor protection depends on your browser or network setup.
messages.sweep.balanceRead.noRpc: No RPC is configured for this chain in Settings, so the balance was not read and no balance request was made.
messages.sweep.balanceRead.settingsChanged: Not read: the RPC or scan privacy settings changed in another tab after this page opened. Nothing was sent. Open Sweep again to read the balance with the current settings.
messages.sweep.balanceNotRead: not read yet (press the button below)
messages.sweep.reviewChanged: The review changed while signing, before handoff. No transaction or order was sent. Review and sign again.
messages.sweep.routeChanged: Nothing was sent: the RPC, relayer or scan privacy settings changed in another tab after this page opened. Open Sweep again to continue with the current settings.

messages.sellerKeys.keystoreDownloaded: Encrypted keystore downloaded. Keep the file and remember the passphrase: neither can be recovered. Then verify the backup below with that file; until then the idle lock keeps these keys loaded.
messages.sellerKeys.notKeystore: This is not a GhostPay keystore file.
messages.sellerKeys.keystoreDecrypted: Keystore decrypted; keys are in memory.
messages.sellerKeys.vaultSaved: Encrypted seller vault saved in this browser. The passphrase was cleared.
messages.sellerKeys.vaultUnlocked: Encrypted vault unlocked. Seller keys are back in memory.
messages.sellerKeys.vaultDeleted: Encrypted vault deleted from this browser.
messages.sellerKeys.keystoreReceived: Encrypted keystore received. Enter its passphrase and choose Decrypt and load.
messages.sellerKeys.title: Seller keys
messages.sellerKeys.memory.title: Keys stay in memory by default
messages.sellerKeys.memory.body: Keys are generated and used only inside this page. They are never written to browser storage unless you explicitly save the optional encrypted vault below. Reloading or closing the tab forgets keys that were not saved. The idle lock in Settings also wipes keys from memory, but only keys that can be loaded again: all three imported keys, downloaded as a keystore and verified, or saved in the vault.
messages.sellerKeys.checkingVault: Checking for an encrypted seller vault…
messages.sellerKeys.storageUnavailable.title: Encrypted browser storage is unavailable
messages.sellerKeys.storageUnavailable.body: This browser cannot read the optional vault. In-memory key use and encrypted file backups remain available, but do not try to save a local vault here.
messages.sellerKeys.vaultSavedHeading: Encrypted seller vault saved in this browser
messages.sellerKeys.unlockExplain: Unlocking replaces the keys currently in memory. The vault stores only the encrypted keystore text; GhostPay never stores your passphrase.
messages.sellerKeys.vaultNoBrowserSave: Do not let your browser or password manager save this passphrase, even when it offers to: anyone using this browser profile could then unlock the vault, which defeats the vault and the idle lock.
messages.sellerKeys.deleteSoleCopy: This vault may be the only copy. To permanently delete it, type “{phrase}”.
messages.sellerKeys.deleteExplain: This permanently deletes the saved ciphertext in this browser. Keep a separate backup first if needed.
messages.sellerKeys.deleteHolds: This vault holds the seller keys of meta-address:
messages.sellerKeys.deleteLoaded: These are the keys loaded now. Enter this vault’s passphrase to delete it.
messages.sellerKeys.deleteOther: These are not the keys loaded now.
messages.sellerKeys.deleteUnreadable: This record is not a valid keystore, so its meta-address cannot be shown.
messages.sellerKeys.unlockReplaces.title: The keys loaded now have no backup
messages.sellerKeys.unlockReplaces.body: Unlocking the saved vault replaces them, and every payment sent to their meta-address can then never be swept. Back them up first unless you are sure they hold nothing.
messages.sellerKeys.unlockReplacesSignerOnly.titl: The signing key loaded now has no backup
messages.sellerKeys.unlockReplacesSignerOnly.body: Unlocking the saved vault replaces the loaded keys. Payments to their meta-address stay sweepable with the spending and viewing keys you imported, but the invoice-signing key generated here is lost: nothing can be signed with it again, not even receipts for the invoices it signed. Back the keys up first unless you do not need that key.
messages.sellerKeys.stepUp.label: Passphrase of the vault these keys are tied to
messages.sellerKeys.stepUp.hint: These keys were unlocked from, saved to or found in an encrypted vault in this browser, so that vault’s passphrase is needed before they are exported or saved under a new passphrase, even if the vault has been deleted since.
messages.sellerKeys.signKey.label: Invoice-signing private key (optional)
messages.sellerKeys.signKey.hint: Leave empty to generate a new invoice-signing key. To keep that signer, save the encrypted vault or download and verify a seller keystore. Importing the same two hex keys again produces a different signer. Each of the three keys must be distinct.
messages.sellerKeys.metaShare: Share this to receive payments. It reveals no private key.
messages.sellerKeys.payersSee: “signature matches key …”. They can pin this key; an unpinned key identifies nobody.
messages.sellerKeys.suggested: Suggested: {words} random words picked on this device ({bits} bits). Write it down, then type it again below, or replace it with your own.
messages.sellerKeys.formatNote: Format: scrypt (N=2^17, r=8, p=1) and AES-256-GCM. GhostPay does not store the passphrase anywhere.
messages.sellerKeys.backupSmallerHint: Smaller codes are easier for low-resolution cameras. Scan every part on your other device with GhostPay’s “Import encrypted keystore QR”. Each part is still secret.
messages.sellerKeys.forgetQr: Forget encrypted QR from this page
messages.sellerKeys.vaultExplain: This keeps an encrypted keystore in this browser’s IndexedDB so you can unlock after reload. Anyone with access to this browser profile can copy the ciphertext and attempt offline guesses; choose a strong passphrase. Browser storage can be cleared or lost, so keep a separate backup. GhostPay never saves the passphrase or plaintext key material here.
messages.sellerKeys.saveVault: Save encrypted vault in this browser
messages.sellerKeys.vaultExists: A vault already exists. It is never overwritten automatically; unlock or explicitly delete it before saving a different key set.
messages.sellerKeys.wipeUnsaved.title: Wipe keys that have no backup?
messages.sellerKeys.wipeUnsaved.body: No copy of these keys exists outside this tab. Wiping them loses them for good, and every payment sent to their meta-address can then never be swept. Back them up first unless you are sure they hold nothing.
messages.sellerKeys.wipeSignerOnly.title: Wipe keys whose signing key has no backup?
messages.sellerKeys.wipeSignerOnly.body: Payments to their meta-address stay sweepable with the spending and viewing keys you imported, but the invoice-signing key generated here exists only in this tab. Once it is wiped, nothing can be signed with it again, not even receipts for the invoices it signed. Back the keys up first unless you do not need that key.
messages.sellerKeys.wipeHint: This removes the keys from this tab only. Scan checkpoints, scan history, local tags and any saved vault stay in this browser, and anyone with this browser profile and your meta-address can tell from them that these keys were used here. To remove them, clear this site’s data in your browser settings, after backing up what you need.
messages.sellerKeys.registryHint: Publishing your meta-address to the ERC-6538 registry would publicly associate it with your wallet address. Publishing is optional and has its own page.
messages.backupGate.title: Back up these seller keys first
messages.backupGate.body: Invoices and the meta-address invite payments that only these keys can sweep, and the keys exist only in this tab. If it closes or the browser crashes before you back them up, those payments are lost for good.
messages.backupGate.signerOnly.body: Payments stay sweepable with the spending and viewing keys you imported, but invoices are signed with an invoice-signing key that exists only in this tab. If it closes, reloads or crashes before you back them up, nothing can be signed with that key again, not even receipts for the invoices it signed.
messages.backupGate.waiverLabel: To continue without a backup, type: {phrase}
messages.app.backup.title: These seller keys have no backup
messages.app.backup.body: They exist only in this tab. If it closes, reloads or crashes before you back them up, every payment sent to their meta-address is lost. Until then the idle lock leaves them loaded.
messages.app.backup.signerOnly.title: The invoice-signing key has no backup
messages.app.backup.signerOnly.body: Payments to your meta-address stay sweepable with the spending and viewing keys you imported. The invoice-signing key was generated in this tab and exists nowhere else: once the tab closes, reloads or crashes, nothing can be signed with it again, not even receipts for the invoices it signed.
messages.app.idle.wiped: Seller keys wiped from memory and local tags locked after inactivity.
messages.app.idle.kept: Local tags locked after inactivity. Seller keys stay loaded because they have no backup yet.
messages.app.idle.wipedNotice: Seller keys were wiped from memory after {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} without activity. Load them again under Seller keys from your keystore file, the browser vault or your hex keys.
messages.app.idle.signerLost: The invoice-signing key generated when the hex keys were imported had no backup and is gone: loading them again generates a new one.
messages.settings.outside.title: Settings can be changed outside this page
messages.settings.outside.body: Anything that can write to this site’s browser storage, including another local user, malware or an extension, can change these RPC, relayer and pinned-signer settings. Review the endpoints and signer keys before relying on them. A second RPC can reveal disagreements, but it does not make either provider trustworthy by itself.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.errWindow: Window size must be a whole number of blocks from 0 to 100000.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.errDelays: Delays must be whole milliseconds, minimum at most maximum, up to 10000.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.errBudget: The per-scan budget must be from 1 to 100000.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.saved: Scan privacy settings saved. They apply to the next scan.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.refused: This browser refused to store the scan privacy settings.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.hint: These options change how announcements are fetched, not what is on-chain. A web page cannot open a SOCKS connection or check that it runs in Tor Browser: “Tor Browser” means you opened this page in Tor Browser yourself; “Local proxy” means a JSON-RPC forwarder you run on this computer (for example one that sends traffic over Tor). Defaults add no new destination.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.requireProxy: Require the private path (block the scan instead of falling back; skip the direct second RPC behind a local proxy)
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.endpointRequired: Required: an address on 127.0.0.1 or localhost.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.endpointOptional: Optional: leave empty to use the RPC above.

messages.settings.scanLanes.flood: Flood threshold (announcements per caller per block)
messages.settings.scanLanes.floodHint: A caller posting more than this many announcements in one block is treated as likely spam: those announcements are checked last, never skipped. Announcements posted by the GhostPay router are never treated as spam.
messages.settings.scanLanes.score: Check suspected spam last (local score: repeated ephemeral keys, floods, malformed metadata)
messages.settings.scanLanes.transfers: Estimate same-token transfers for the privacy set (costs RPC calls)
messages.settings.scanLanes.transfersHint: Off by default. When on, each scan ends by asking the scan RPC for the recent Transfer logs of the token you were last paid in, over the last {blocks} blocks, with no sender or recipient in the request, and counts those at a similar amount (within 25%). The provider learns which token you scan for and when; this request names none of your addresses. The result is a labelled estimate and never changes the privacy-set level; any provider limit or error shows it as unknown.
messages.settings.scanLanes.matchCover: Blur which payments matched among other lookups (costs more RPC calls)
messages.settings.scanLanes.matchCoverHint: Off by default. Checking a matched router payment asks your RPC (and a second provider, if set) for that payment’s block, receipt and transaction, which tells the provider which public announcement was yours. When on, every scan also checks about half of the other router payments in supported tokens that it reads, whether or not any payment matched, the same way and in chain order, and discards their results; your payments are verified exactly as before. Which others are checked is fixed by a key only you hold, so a rescan, a resumed scan or a scan after a reorg checks the same ones. This makes it harder for a provider that only records requests to tell which lookups were yours. It does not stop a provider that alters or fails its answers from finding out. It does not cover reading a balance, exporting a payment key or sweeping through the same RPC, re-checking one payment from the result list, or the extra block reads after a reorg or a failed check, and it does not hide when you scanned or your IP address. With few router payments there is little or no cover. It costs many more RPC calls, in proportion to how busy the chain is.
messages.scanLanes.disclosure.matchCover: With cover lookups on: about half of the other router payments each scan reads are looked up the same way as yours, whether or not anything matched. The provider can still find out which payment matched if it alters or fails its answers, after a reorg or a failed check, or if you later read its balance, export its key or sweep it through this RPC.

messages.about.title: About and privacy
messages.about.intro: GhostPay creates one-time (stealth) addresses so that a seller’s receiving address is not published. It is a static page: there is no GhostPay server, account or analytics, and it loads no third-party code or fonts.
messages.about.feeNote: Gas-sponsored sweeps charge max(110 % of the gas cost, 0.5 % of the amount), capped at 3 %, shown in the quote before you sign. The optional gas buffer and the delay are free.
messages.about.verify.title: How to verify this release
messages.about.verify.intro: The SHA-256 on Home is informational: this page computes it from a script fetched from the same host. A compromised host could serve both the app and the hash it wants you to see, so that check does not establish that the release is authentic.
messages.about.verify.step1: Download the published release and its checksum from a second channel, then verify the files locally with the published SHA256SUMS.
messages.about.verify.step2: When a release key is built into this app, the deployment manifest must have a valid signature from one of those keys. That signature only helps if you have verified the app bundle itself.
messages.about.verify.step3: Check that the deployment addresses and code match the chain through an RPC you trust. A second independent RPC can expose disagreements, but agreement alone does not prove either provider is honest.
messages.about.verify.step4: Before sending, check that the final screen and your wallet show the same contract, one-time address, amounts and fee recipient.
messages.about.verify.step5: Hosting headers such as CSP and Referrer-Policy only apply on hosts that support them; static hosts may not be able to enforce every policy.

messages.create.buffer.label: Gas buffer policy

messages.create.buffer.error.min: Enter the minimum buffer as a whole number of wei from 1 to 2^256-1, digits only.
messages.create.buffer.error.max: Enter the maximum buffer as a whole number of wei from 1 to 2^256-1, digits only.
messages.create.buffer.error.order: The maximum buffer must be at least the minimum buffer.
messages.create.buffer.error.cap: The minimum buffer is above the {capNative} native coin safety cap that payers apply ({capWei} wei), so no payer could meet it. Enter a smaller minimum.
messages.create.buffer.nativeHint: Gas buffers only apply to token invoices. A native-coin invoice never carries a buffer policy, so it stays a standard invoice that lean builds can pay.
messages.scan.title: Scan and receive
messages.scan.needKeys: Load or generate seller keys first.
messages.scan.intro: Announcements are downloaded from your RPC and checked inside a dedicated worker. The worker gets public logs and your viewing key for this scan only; it cannot reach the network.
messages.scan.rpcPrivacy.title: RPC privacy
messages.scan.rpcPrivacy.body: Your RPC provider sees your IP address, scan ranges, and logs. Verifying a router payment also requests token transfer logs filtered for the one-time address, or the transaction receipt; these requests can reveal which public announcements matched your keys. A configured second provider sees the same verification evidence. Use trusted private RPC providers or your own nodes if this matters to you.
messages.scan.disclosure.summary: What each party learns with your scan privacy settings
messages.scan.disclosure.hint: Change the scan transport, windows and delays in Settings. None of these options hides anything on-chain.

messages.scan.autoRescan: Keep checking for new payments while this page is open
messages.scan.autoRescan.hint: Off by default. When on, after a scan finishes cleanly GhostPay resumes from the checkpoint about every 60 to 90 seconds, only while this tab is visible and the same keys and chain are selected. Your RPC provider can see the timing of these repeated requests. Closing the tab, locking, cancelling or any error stops it; nothing runs in the background or on a server.
messages.scan.autoRescan.stopped: Automatic checking stopped because the last scan did not finish cleanly. Fix the problem above and start a scan again.

messages.scan.error.noManifest: Payments are disabled on this chain: no deployment manifest is loaded, so the announcer address is unknown.
messages.scan.lag: The second RPC reports block {secondary}, {behind} blocks behind the scan RPC (block {head}). Each scan stops at the last block both providers have, so later payments appear only once the second RPC catches up. Check it in Settings if this persists.
messages.scan.routerOnly: {single, select, yes {Block {list} held} other {Blocks {list} held}} more announcements than one RPC response may carry (likely announcement spam). messages.pay.scan.needsPassphrase: This invoice needs a passphrase. Its header is unverified until it opens.
messages.pay.scan.chainValid: Chain {chain}. The embedded key signed this invoice; this does not establish seller identity.
messages.pay.scan.chainInvalid: Chain {chain}. The invoice signature is invalid. Payment will remain blocked.
messages.pay.scan.openNote: Opening shows the ordinary invoice review. It does not connect a wallet or submit a payment.
messages.pay.paste.hintLocal: The link is read in this page only. It is never sent to a server.
messages.pay.paste.hintHistory: Pasting is safer than clicking: a browser may keep a clicked invoice URL, including its secret part, in its history even after this page removes it from the address bar. Copy the link and paste it here, or open it in a private window.
messages.pay.fiatNotChecked: (not converted or checked by this app)
messages.pay.pricing.quote: Fiat quote from {source}, taken {taken}, valid until {until}, max slippage {slippage} %. Not a guaranteed fiat value.

messages.pay.receipt.heading: Import a seller receipt
messages.pay.receipt.intro: This checks the receipt signature against the current signed invoice, chain, asset and exact seller amount. If this page has a transaction hash or prepared one-time address, those are checked too. A seller signature proves control of a key and does not independently prove an on-chain payment or seller identity.
messages.pay.receipt.privacy: A receipt may reveal a private amount, transaction and invoice association on this screen.
messages.pay.receipt.consent: I consent to opening private receipt details on this screen.

messages.pay.receipt.matchTrustedKey: The signature matches the explicitly trusted key you entered, and the invoice digest, chain, asset and seller amount match. This is a seller-key attestation, not independent payment proof.

messages.pay.delay.label: Wait a random time first ({min} to {max} minutes)
messages.pay.delay.hint: Timing friction only, not anonymity. While waiting nothing is signed or sent, and the page must stay open. You can cancel or send now.
messages.pay.buffer.notAccepted: The seller does not accept a gas buffer for this invoice.

messages.pay.buffer.estimate: Extra {amount} {native} (native, not {symbol}) is sent in the same transaction to the one-time address. This publicly links your payment, the one-time address and the buffer. It is an estimate ({gas} gas{source, select, simulated {, from a simulated token transfer} other {, default table value until you prepare the payment}} at up to {fee} wei, +20 %), not a guarantee.{raised, select, yes { Raised to the seller's minimum buffer for this invoice.} other {}} It is never refunded.

messages.pay.status.unverified: Status: unverified. A transaction with this hash is in block {block}, but it was not compared with the preview, so this app does not report it as this payment.
messages.pay.receipt.download.confirm: This receipt contains the amount and time of your payment. Keep it private. Download?

messages.reuse.sameInvoice: This tab already prepared this exact destination for the same signed invoice. messages.reuse.differentInvoice: This account already prepared this exact destination for another invoice on this network in this tab. messages.reuse.sweep: You previously submitted a sweep to this destination from this seller profile on this network in this tab. If you intended to use the same wallet, you can continue. Transfers to it can be linked on-chain.
messages.reuse.unavailable: Local destination history is unavailable for this review. You can still continue.
messages.reuse.walletChanged: The wallet account or network may have changed, or you left this page, so this review no longer compares destination history. Reopen the invoice and connect again to compare.
messages.reuse.invoiceMeta: You can use the same seller meta-address on multiple invoices. The payer derives the payment destination at checkout.
messages.reuse.sweepOtherProfile: You previously submitted a sweep to this destination from a different seller profile on this network in this tab. Sweeping here again links those seller profiles on-chain. Use a fresh destination if they should stay separate.
messages.reuse.ownPayment: This destination is another one-time address announced as a payment to these keys in this scan. Sweeping into it links both payments on-chain, and whoever paid that address can see the funds arrive. Use a fresh destination if that matters.
messages.pay.final.feeLine: {amount} {symbol} to {recipient} (deployment manifest verified against the chain)
messages.pay.approval.explain: Pressing the button first asks your wallet for this exact approval and then for the payment. Check the amount in your wallet: it must not be unlimited. messages.disclosure.fee.signed: GhostPay charges {pct} % on payments made through its checkout contract. The fee goes to {#mono}{recipient}{/mono} (shown from the deployment manifest, whose signature was verified by a release key built into this app). Paying the stealth address directly costs no GhostPay fee.
messages.disclosure.fee.unsigned: GhostPay charges {pct} % on payments made through its checkout contract. The fee goes to {#mono}{recipient}{/mono} (shown from the deployment manifest, which is unsigned and permitted only as a testnet development manifest). Paying the stealth address directly costs no GhostPay fee.
messages.disclosure.fee.unavailable: GhostPay charges {pct} % on payments made through its checkout contract. The fee goes to {#mono}{recipient}{/mono} (shown from the deployment manifest, with signature status unavailable). Paying the stealth address directly costs no GhostPay fee.
messages.disclosure.fee.loading: GhostPay charges {pct} % on payments made through its checkout contract. The fee goes to the address in the deployment manifest (loading…). Paying the stealth address directly costs no GhostPay fee.
messages.disclosure.fee.none: GhostPay charges {pct} % on payments made through its checkout contract. The fee goes to the address in the deployment manifest, but {chain} has none loaded: {#strong}payments disabled on this chain{/strong}. Paying the stealth address directly costs no GhostPay fee.
messages.disclosure.observer.1.learns: Payer address, token, gross and net amounts, the fee flow to the fee recipient, router use, the announcement (stealth address, ephemeral key, view tag), timing, and the sweep source and destination if swept in the clear.
messages.disclosure.observer.1.not: Seller identity from the stealth address alone; invoice contents.
messages.disclosure.observer.2.learns: Client IP, user agent, which app files were fetched, timing.
messages.disclosure.observer.2.not: The URL fragment, keys, invoice contents.
messages.disclosure.observer.3.learns: Client IP, queried block ranges and addresses, submitted transactions.
messages.disclosure.observer.3.not: Viewing or spending keys (never sent); invoice contents.
messages.disclosure.observer.4.learns: Your IP address (hashed by the reference relayer for rate limits, but visible to the operator and any proxy), the stealth address, destination, token, amount, fee, timing; can censor.
messages.disclosure.observer.6.learns: The entire invoice (it is a bearer link).
messages.disclosure.observer.7.not: Payer or seller identity beyond public chain data.
messages.disclosure.limit.1: GhostPay does not hide the payer, the amount, the token, the time, or the router call. It hides which seller owns the one-time (stealth) address.
messages.disclosure.limit.2: A sweep from a stealth address to a known wallet links them on-chain. Sweeping through a relayer does not remove that link.
messages.disclosure.limit.3: An invoice link is a bearer secret: anyone who has the link (or its QR code) can read it. The signature only shows the link was not altered by someone without the signing key; it does not prove who the seller is.
messages.disclosure.limit.4: The optional delay is timing friction, not anonymity: no cover transactions are created and the final transaction is public.
messages.disclosure.limit.5: The optional gas buffer is a public native transfer in the same transaction as your payment and links the payer to the stealth address.
messages.disclosure.limit.6: This app runs entirely in your browser, but your browser, extensions, wallet, RPC provider and operating system are all trusted by it. It has had no external audit.

messages.tagArchive.passphrase.suggested: Suggested: {words} random words picked on this device ({bits} bits). Write it down, then type it again below, or replace it with your own.
messages.tagArchive.format: Format: scrypt (N=2^17, r=8, p=1) and AES-256-GCM, .gpa file with a fixed name that never contains labels. The archive holds your tags, not your keys. messages.tagArchive.rotate.heading: Rotate tag keys

messages.help.rpc: An RPC provider supplies blockchain data and sees the network requests sent to it. A second, independent provider can reveal disagreements and improve availability, but it also shares those requests with another operator. A successful endpoint test checks the reported chain id only; it does not certify the provider or verify a payment.
messages.help.keystoreFile: Choose the original encrypted GhostPay keystore JSON downloaded from Seller keys. It contains encrypted private keys and requires its matching passphrase. The format and size are checked locally before decryption. A public seller config, receipt or tag archive cannot restore these keys. A refused file leaves the current keys unchanged; choose the correct file and retry.
messages.help.tagArchiveFile: Choose the encrypted .gpa file downloaded by Download encrypted tag archive. It contains private labels and optional encrypted history, but no seller private keys. Enter the archive passphrase to preview it locally, then review Merge or Replace before applying. A keystore, receipt, public config or invalid archive is refused without applying an import.
messages.help.ledgerBackupFile: Choose the encrypted reconciliation JSON exported for this seller and chain. Restoring it needs the same seller viewing key. It contains encrypted observations, invoice registrations and receipts; it is not a seller-key backup. Preview checks the format and scope before activation. Restored observations remain historical until rescanned.
messages.help.sellerConfigFile: Choose the public seller-config JSON exported from your other device. GhostPay checks the schema, public keys and supported chain ids, then shows an untrusted preview. Compare both screens before using it. This file contains no private keys, grants no signing authority and cannot restore a keystore or encrypted history.
messages.help.receiptFile: Choose a signed GhostPay receipt JSON saved by the seller. Verification checks its signature and exact invoice, chain, asset, amount and recipient binding when the required invoice context is available. A valid signature proves control of the signing key; it does not establish the seller's identity or independently prove that a payment is confirmed on chain.
messages.help.receiptQr: The QR is a representation of the serialized receipt, not additional evidence. Save the original digital receipt JSON whenever possible. A cropped, unreadable or incomplete QR image may lose information, and neither the image nor the JSON adds independent payment verification. Both expose the receipt's transaction, recipient, amount and invoice digest.
messages.help.receiptInvoiceFile: Choose the original text file containing the signed invoice link or fragment supplied by the seller or downloaded when the invoice was created. It may reveal invoice details or an encrypted bearer link. GhostPay validates the format, signature and payment binding locally; an encrypted invoice also needs its passphrase. A receipt JSON or another file type is refused.
messages.help.archiveMode: Merge keeps unrelated local tags and previews updates from the archive. Replace can remove local tags omitted from the archive. Neither mode applies anything until you review and approve the preview. Scan-history stores commit separately; if an import is interrupted, inspect the reported outcome and make a new preview before retrying.
messages.help.merchantRegistration: Registration stores a minimal local invoice record for later matching with eligible scan observations. It does not publish the invoice or mark it paid. A proposed match still needs your explicit confirmation. Back up seller keys and local records separately; public device pairing cannot restore either secret keys or encrypted history.

messages.btc.verification.check.header: The block header hash equals the hash the server reported, and the header meets its own proof-of-work target and the network limit.
messages.btc.verification.check.transactions: Transaction ids are recomputed on this device and must produce the header Merkle root, so inputs and outputs are bound to the header.
messages.btc.verification.check.witness: Witness data is bound to the header through the coinbase witness commitment (BIP-141), so input keys cannot be swapped.
messages.btc.verification.check.chain: Block headers from the server are checked on this device starting at the pinned genesis block: each must link to the one before, meet its proof-of-work target, carry the difficulty the network rules require, and have a valid timestamp and version. Among competing branches the one with the most cumulative work is kept. Every scanned block must have the hash this checked chain has at its height, so a block that extends nothing, or sits on a branch with less work, is refused.
messages.btc.verification.check.storage: Checked headers are saved in this browser and checked again in full when loaded; saved headers that fail any check are discarded and downloaded again. When a chain with more work replaces blocks that were already scanned, the results from those blocks are removed.
messages.btc.verification.limit.validation: This is header-chain validation against the chain the server claims is best, with most-work selection among the headers it sent. It is not SPV and not full validation: no transaction or script is validated beyond the checks above. A server can hide a heavier chain or show you only its own (an eclipse), and proof of work on test networks is cheap, so a server can mine a heavier fork itself.
messages.btc.verification.limit.prevouts: The scripts and amounts of the outputs being spent come from the server (they live in earlier blocks). A lying server can hide a payment, and with a fork it mined itself (cheap on test networks) it can also invent one. Confirm a payment with a source you trust before relying on it.
messages.btc.verification.limit.spent: Spent status is derived on this device from the inputs of the scanned blocks (a spend still in the mempool, or one in a block scanned before spend tracking, is not visible); only the optional provider check asks the server per outpoint and reveals this wallet's outputs.

messages.btc.oracle.urlHint: Choose a separate server with the full, unfiltered index for this exact network. HTTP routes are legacy; gRPC-Web requires a compatible HTTPS proxy.
messages.btc.oracle.fullHelp: Full-block mode downloads and verifies Esplora blocks, then compares every block's complete tweaks and outputs with the oracle. A disagreement stops the scan. This does not reduce block-download bandwidth.
messages.btc.oracle.light: Use light oracle scans with transaction inclusion proofs
messages.btc.oracle.lightHelp: The oracle supplies scan data. Every matched output requires a raw-transaction and Merkle inclusion proof against the checked header chain before it can be swept. The oracle can still omit payments; the proof server learns which transaction IDs match your wallet.
messages.btc.oracle.disclosure: Selected servers learn your IP and requested block ranges. They never receive scan or spend keys. Different URLs do not prove that operators are independent. Requests begin only when you start a check or scan.
messages.btc.oracle.secondEnable: Compare every scanned block with a second oracle
messages.btc.oracle.lightChecks: Light mode recomputes each matched transaction ID and verifies its exact taproot output, amount and Merkle inclusion against the checked header hash. It does not verify witness data, previous outputs, scripts or full-block consensus.
messages.btc.oracle.lightLimits: Inclusion proofs do not prove that the oracle supplied every payment or that the server showed the best chain. A second oracle can expose disagreement but colluding servers can still omit data. Spent status remains the Esplora server's report.
messages.btc.oracle.resultsNote: Results passed the selected proof and source checks. Different endpoints are not proof of independent operators; header withholding and omitted oracle data remain limitations. If you enabled the provider spent check, spent status is that provider's report.
messages.policy.create.withdrawableAny: This policy has no limits: it can withdraw any token and the native coin.
messages.policy.create.withdrawableOnly: This policy can withdraw only: {tokens}. A payment in any other token or coin stays locked in the account forever, and payers cannot see your limits in the meta-address: tell them which assets to use.
messages.policy.pay.coverageUnknownTitle: This app cannot check that the payee can withdraw this asset
messages.policy.pay.coverageUnknown: A policy meta-address carries only a hash of the payee's policy, not its per-token limits. If the policy has limits and none for this asset, the payment stays locked in the policy account forever and nobody can recover it. Pay only in an asset the payee has confirmed over a channel you trust.

messages.policy.pay.tokenNotWithdrawable: Blocked: the payee's policy record loaded in this tab has per-token limits and none for this asset, so the policy account could never withdraw it. Nothing was sent.
messages.policy.pay.committedAssetNotWithdrawable: Blocked: a loaded record matches the payee's policy commitment and its immutable limits do not cover this asset. The policy account cannot withdraw it. Nothing was sent.

messages.stealthExport.details.ownership.title: Key ownership
messages.stealthExport.details.ownership.body: Your keys control this address. This is not payment confirmation or finality.
messages.stealthExport.details.futureDeposits: A private key keeps control of its address after the funds there are swept, including any future deposits to it. Anyone who also has your private viewing key and this payment’s public announcement can reconstruct your master spending key and spend your other discoverable scheme-1 payments. The payer who made this payment can do the same without your viewing key, so never send this payment’s private key to the payer, for example as a refund; send funds instead.
messages.stealthExport.details.public.heading: Public record
messages.stealthExport.details.public.hint: A ghostpay-stealth-public-v1 file with the address, its public key and the announcement locator. It holds no secret.
messages.stealthExport.details.public.done: Public record generated; download initiated. This file contains no private keys.
messages.stealthExport.details.rpcPrivacy: Secret exports check this payment address for contract code through the RPC used by this scan. That provider can associate the address, the request time and your connecting IP. No private key is sent. Export only if you accept this disclosure.
messages.stealthExport.details.encrypted.heading: Encrypted keypair
messages.stealthExport.details.encrypted.hint: The one-time private key is encrypted with your new passphrase. The network, address, public key and announcement details remain readable in the file. You can recover the key offline with the reference script.
messages.stealthExport.details.encrypted.done: Encrypted keypair generated; download initiated. Keep and verify the saved file.
messages.stealthExport.details.raw.heading: Raw private key
messages.stealthExport.details.raw.hint: A plain-text file with this payment’s EVM private key, for wallets that import a private key. It is never shown on screen or copied.
messages.stealthExport.raw.confirm.title: Download a plain-text private key?
messages.stealthExport.raw.confirm.body: The file holds this payment’s private key unencrypted. Anyone who gets it can spend funds at this address, now and in the future. Anyone who also has your private viewing key and this payment’s public announcement can reconstruct your master spending key and spend your other discoverable scheme-1 payments. The payer who made this payment can do the same without your viewing key, so never send this file or key to the payer, for example as a refund; send funds instead. Browser downloads can leave copies on disk, in backups and in search indexes. This is a single EVM private key, not a seed or recovery phrase; by itself, it controls this address and does not discover other stealth payments.
messages.stealthExport.raw.done: Private key file generated; download initiated. Confirm that you saved it. Keep it offline and delete it when you no longer need it.
messages.stealthExport.verify.heading: Keep and verify this backup
messages.stealthExport.verify.generated: Encrypted file generated; download has not started. Retry the download, then keep and verify the saved file.
messages.stealthExport.verify.downloadStarted: File generated; download initiated. Retention and recoverability are not yet confirmed.
messages.stealthExport.verify.retained: You confirmed keeping this backup. Recoverability is not yet verified.
messages.stealthExport.verify.savedSuccess: Saved backup verified. This exact exported file decrypted successfully and its keys match their public identities.
messages.stealthExport.verify.scope: Verification applies only to this file. It does not mark the complete seller keystore as backed up.
messages.stealthExport.verify.keep: I saved this backup file and kept its passphrase separately.
messages.stealthExport.verify.differentFile: This is not the exact file generated by this export. Choose the saved copy of this download, or use Check export without importing to check another backup.
messages.error.paymentKeyExport.noPayments: There are no payments to export.
messages.error.paymentKeyExport.recoveredKeysClos: This export was closed and its keys were wiped. Open the file again.
messages.error.paymentKeyExport.publicRecordIsNot: A public record contains no private keys and cannot be verified as a recoverable backup.
messages.stealthExport.archive.heading: Export all payment keys (encrypted)
messages.stealthExport.archive.summary: {count, plural, one {# payment key} other {# payment keys}} found on {chain}, scope: all discovered payments.
messages.stealthExport.archive.hint: Private keys are encrypted with a new passphrase (ghostpay-stealth-keypair-v1). The authenticated public header stays readable without the passphrase: it exposes the chain, payment count, every included address and public key, and announcement locators, linking all archive entries. Master keys are not included. Keep decrypted payment keys away from anyone who holds your private viewing key: together with a payment’s public announcement, they allow reconstruction of your master spending key. Before export, every address is checked for contract code through the RPC this scan used.
messages.stealthExport.archive.rpcPrivacy: Before the download, every address in this archive is checked for contract code through the RPC this scan used. That provider can link all of these addresses to each other, to the request time and to your connecting IP. No private key is sent. Export only if you accept this disclosure.
messages.stealthExport.archive.done: Encrypted payment key archive generated; download initiated. Keep and verify the saved file.
messages.stealthExport.master.heading: Master stealth key backup (encrypted)
messages.stealthExport.master.body: Exports your master spending and viewing keys, encrypted with a new passphrase, in the documented ghostpay-stealth-master-v1 format (scheme 1, derivation eip5564-scheme1-adr0001). With scheme-compatible tooling (GhostPay or the reference recovery script) they recover every discoverable past and future payment to your meta-address, including payments missing from any payment key archive. A generic wallet cannot use them directly. The invoice-signing key is not included: keep your keystore backup for it.
messages.stealthExport.master.done: Master backup generated; download initiated. Keep and verify the saved file.
messages.stealthExport.open.heading: Open a stealth key export
messages.stealthExport.open.body: Opens a GhostPay stealth key export (public record, payment keys or master backup) in this browser, without the original installation, site or account. The file is read and decrypted here; nothing is uploaded.
messages.stealthExport.open.passphraseHint: Not needed for a public record.
messages.stealthExport.open.close: Close the export and wipe its keys
messages.stealthExport.open.public.title: Public payment record
messages.stealthExport.open.public.body: This file holds no key and proves no ownership. Apart from its public key matching its address, its contents are only as trustworthy as the place the file came from.
messages.stealthExport.open.keypair.title: Verified payment keys
messages.stealthExport.open.keypair.summary: {count, plural, one {# payment key} other {# payment keys}} on {chain}, scope: {scope}. Every key was checked against its address.
messages.stealthExport.open.master.title: Verified master keys
messages.stealthExport.open.master.body: Spending and viewing keys of this meta-address. Loading them lets this browser scan for and sweep every payment to it. A new invoice-signing key is generated, because a master backup never holds one.
messages.stealthExport.open.master.load: Load these spending and viewing keys
messages.stealthExport.open.master.loaded: These spending and viewing keys are already loaded.
messages.stealthExport.open.master.done: Spending and viewing keys loaded from the master backup, with a new invoice-signing key. Back the keys up in Seller keys.
messages.stealthExport.open.replace.title: The keys loaded now have no verified backup
messages.stealthExport.open.replace.body: Loading the master keys replaces the loaded keys. Without a backup, every payment sent to their meta-address can then never be swept, and their invoice-signing key is lost. Back them up first unless you are sure they hold nothing.
messages.stealthExport.verify.success: Backup verified. It decrypted successfully and every recovered key matches its public identity. No keys were imported.
messages.stealthExport.verify.masterScope: This backup restores spending and viewing keys only. It does not include the invoice-signing key.
messages.stealthExport.open.replace.savedBody: A recoverable copy of the current keys was found. Confirm before replacing this wallet with the selected master backup.
messages.retention.title: Invoice preview retention
messages.retention.label: Clear generated invoice previews automatically
messages.retention.scope: Applies only to generated invoice details currently shown on this page. Copy the link first: once a preview is closed, this page cannot show that link again. Nothing runs after closing the app. Saved invoices, transaction history, keys and recovery data are excluded.
messages.retention.preserved: This clears only screen previews; a link you have not copied cannot be shown again. It does not revoke shared invoice links or remove saved invoices, pending payments, vaults, backups or security records.
messages.retention.storage: The preference could not be saved. No cleanup policy was changed.
messages.retention.stale: Screen data changed. Preview cleanup again.
messages.retention.failed: Some screen data could not be cleared. Preview cleanup again.
messages.retention.proof.title: Payment proof preview retention
messages.retention.proof.label: Close payment proof previews automatically
messages.retention.proof.scope: Closes only the shown QR and text of a payment your RPC reported as included and matching the review. Pending or unverified proofs stay open. Original payment and receipt records remain available. Nothing runs after closing the app.
messages.retention.proof.preserved: This closes only the displayed QR and text. It does not erase the payment result, transaction history, invoices, vaults, backups or security records. Receipt copy and download remain available.
messages.retention.expired: The invoice preview closed under your retention setting. Links you copied still work; this page cannot show that link again.
messages.retention.proof.expired: The payment proof preview closed under your retention setting. Show it again at any time; receipt copy and download remain available.
messages.retention.settings.where: To close previews now, use the preview button on the page that shows them: Create invoice or Pay.
messages.app.idle.suspended.title: Session locked after inactivity
messages.app.idle.suspended.body: Protected operations are locked. Any seller keys still in this tab are retained only for encrypted backup and verification. Save an encrypted browser vault and unlock it, or download and verify a keystore, choose Wipe keys from memory, then import that keystore. These actions use the existing passphrase checks. Anyone with access to this tab can still use this recovery path.
messages.error.session.lockedBackupOnly: The session is locked after inactivity. Back up or verify the retained seller keys, then load them again to continue.
messages.app.idle.keptUnconfirmed: Local tags locked after inactivity. Seller keys are retained because a recoverable copy could not be confirmed.
messages.app.idle.keptSigner: Local tags locked after inactivity. Seller keys stay loaded because the invoice-signing key has no backup.
